methods: Verified SHA-256, byte size, PDF metadata and page counts for all five supplied PDFs.
Rendered every page in source order at 150 DPI and visually inspected all 15 pages; no unreadable pages were found.
Checked embedded text page-by-page. All 15 pages contained usable native text, so OCR was not required; visual inspection confirmed tables, notices, signatures and annotations where present.
Compared normalized page text, page counts and rendered content against the existing published canonical records while preserving each supplied filename and source hash as provenance.
Classified findings by substantive content and traced each source to its existing NPDES, IPP or PFAS catalog record without creating duplicate cards or timeline events.

records.finding: The July 15, 2016 notice identifies Permit GW1010342 for Wexford County Landfill at 990 US Highway 131, Manton, Michigan. DEQ proposed authorization for up to 50,400 gallons per day and 2,000,000 gallons per year of landfill leachate from the evaporator lagoon to ground/groundwater in the southeast quarter of the northeast quarter of Section 33, T23N R09W, Cedar Creek Township. Public comments were due August 15, 2016. The rendered page contains highlighted wording around the proposed issue, evaporator-lagoon source and Cedar Creek location.
records.boundary: This is a proposal and public-comment notice, not proof that final authorization was issued, that discharge occurred, or that groundwater was impacted.

leadTrace.lead: The notice proposes a Rule 2210(y) groundwater discharge for evaporator-lagoon leachate.
leadTrace.targetRecords: Existing NPDES permit, permit-issuance correspondence and Wexford leachate receiving/DMR records
leadTrace.tieBack: Use the final permit and operating records to determine whether the proposal became an authorization and whether any discharge or receiving activity is documented.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: The supplied notice does not itself establish final permit issuance or actual discharge.

records.contentClassification: IPP PFAS screening and sampling workflow
records.finding: The three-page plan establishes the City’s PFAS industrial-user screening workflow: notice and survey responses are generally due within 10 business days; probable sources are notified of intended sampling; sampling is targeted within three months; samples are collected at current IPP monitoring locations, shipped to an approved laboratory and charged to the permit holder. Confirmed significant sources trigger POTW effluent sampling, and effluent results exceeding standards are to be reported to DEQ-WRD within 10 days. The plan also documents reminder procedures for nonresponders, the 4-business-day extension, the June 1, 2018 wastewater sampling guidance and the continuing unavailability of the referenced general guidance as of June 27, 2018. A nonresponsive permit holder is treated as a probable source and receives registered-mail notice of intent to sample.
records.boundary: This is a procedure and decision framework, not evidence that a particular facility was sampled, that a result exceeded a standard, or that the workflow was completed.

leadTrace.lead: The plan directs probable-source sampling and follow-up POTW effluent sampling.
leadTrace.targetRecords: HNF-P7H3-DCN87 interim submission, J17646-1 leachate report, J17993-1 effluent report and related IPP correspondence
leadTrace.tieBack: Compare the planned deadlines and decision points with the dated sampling, analytical and submission records to verify execution rather than infer it from the plan.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: The plan does not report facility-specific sample results or completion dates.

records.finding: The signed May 21, 2018 survey identifies Wexford County Landfill, LLC, representative Vicki Garon, Landfill Engineer. It states that the landfill was accepting waste, that American Waste took ownership in fall 2011, and that industrial waste comprised an estimated 18–30 percent of incoming waste. It says generator names were kept for waste transported by the landfill but not necessarily for other haulers, that SIC-code percentages could not be supplied, and that the landfill had not analyzed its leachate for PFAS at the time of response.
records.boundary: These are respondent statements, not independent sampling, transaction-level hauling records, a laboratory result or proof of PFAS source attribution. The survey’s ownership and information limits are part of the provenance and should not be silently expanded.

leadTrace.lead: The survey’s statement that leachate had not been analyzed for PFAS creates a dated information gap before later sampling.
leadTrace.targetRecords: J17646-1 leachate analytical report and HNJ-P0ZX-8AVDS IPP summary
leadTrace.tieBack: Keep the May 21 respondent statement separate from the October 3 collection and October 29 TestAmerica result; together they show chronology, not a retroactive correction of the survey.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: The survey does not identify all outside-hauler generators or provide a complete waste composition, load history or analytical result.

queueDecision: All five uploads are already represented by canonical public records. Four supplied PDFs are content-equivalent, byte-distinct variants and the SIU/CIU list is byte-identical. The uploads add no new event or analytical result, so no duplicate cards or timeline events were created; supplied filenames and hashes are retained here for provenance.
evidentiaryBoundary: The intake confirms existing public records and strengthens provenance, chronology and lead-tracing. It does not independently establish final groundwater authorization, actual discharge, PFAS concentrations, causal source attribution or compliance beyond the statements and status fields contained in the cited records.
